question: What is a large language model (LLM)?
answer: An LLM is a neural network trained on a lot of text to predict the next piece of text (token). By doing this well it can answer questions, write code and summarise. It does not look facts up by itself and can state wrong things confidently, so important answers need sources or checks.

question: What are tokens and a context window?
answer: Tokens are the small pieces of text a model reads and writes (parts of words). The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can consider at once, including your question, the history and any documents you give it. If the conversation is longer, older parts must be cut or summarised.

question: What does the temperature setting do?
answer: Temperature controls randomness when the model picks the next token. Low values give more predictable, repeatable answers (good for code and tool routing); higher values give more varied, creative answers.

question: What is a hallucination and how can I reduce it?
answer: A hallucination is a fluent answer that is not true or not supported. Reduce it by giving the model trusted source text (RAG) and asking for citations, letting it say 'I don't know', checking numbers and names, and evaluating on questions with known answers.

question: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)?
answer: RAG first searches your own documents or notes for relevant passages and then gives them to the model together with the question, so the answer is based on that text. It lets the assistant use fresh or private information without retraining, and you can show the sources. Retrieved text is untrusted: it may contain hidden instructions.

question: What are embeddings and vector search?
answer: An embedding turns text into a list of numbers so that similar meanings are close together. Vector search finds the stored passages closest to your question's embedding. It finds meaning, not exact words, so combine it with keyword search and check results.

question: When should I fine-tune and when should I use RAG or prompting?
answer: Use prompting first (cheapest). Use RAG when the model needs facts that change or that are private. Fine-tune when you need a consistent style, format or skill (for example always returning a tool-call JSON) that prompting cannot reliably give. Fine-tuning is poor for storing facts and can make the model forget other abilities.

question: What are LoRA and QLoRA?
answer: LoRA fine-tunes a model by training small extra weight matrices instead of all the weights, which needs far less memory and gives a small file you can switch on or off. QLoRA does the same on top of a quantized (compressed) base model so it fits on smaller GPUs. You still need good data and an evaluation set.
reference: Hu et al. 2021 (LoRA); Dettmers et al. 2023 (QLoRA)

question: What is overfitting?
answer: Overfitting means the model learned the training examples (including their quirks) instead of the general pattern, so it scores well on training data and badly on new data. Signs: training score keeps improving while validation score stalls or drops. Fixes: more varied data, simpler model, early stopping, regularisation.

question: What are train / validation / test sets and what is data leakage?
answer: Train data teaches the model, validation data helps you choose settings, and test data is touched only at the end to measure real performance. Leakage is when information from test data sneaks into training (for example near-identical paraphrases on both sides), which makes scores look better than they are. Split by group or source, not randomly by row.

question: What are precision, recall and F1?
answer: Precision: of the things the model flagged, how many were right. Recall: of the things it should have flagged, how many it found. F1 combines both. For a safety filter, missing a dangerous request (low recall) and blocking harmless ones (low precision) are different mistakes; choose what to optimise on purpose.

question: What is class imbalance and why is accuracy misleading?
answer: If 95% of examples are harmless, a model that always says 'harmless' is 95% accurate but useless. Use precision, recall, per-class scores and a confusion matrix, and consider class weights or collecting more examples of the rare class.

question: Why does dataset licensing matter for training?
answer: A dataset's licence says what you may do with it (research only, commercial use, attribution required, no redistribution). Some datasets need you to accept terms or forbid training on certain splits. Record the source and licence of every dataset and never use data whose terms you cannot find.

question: What is quantization (for example GGUF models in Ollama)?
answer: Quantization stores a model's numbers with fewer bits (for example 4-bit instead of 16-bit) so it uses less memory and runs faster on ordinary computers, with some loss of quality. That is how many local models fit on a laptop.

question: What is the advantage of a local model like one run with Ollama?
answer: Your prompts stay on your machine, it works offline and has no per-request fee. The trade-offs are smaller models than the biggest cloud ones, slower speed on weak hardware and you maintain it yourself. Cloud models in a local tool may still send data out, so check which you chose.

question: What is an evaluation harness and why build one before training?
answer: It is a fixed set of test questions with expected results and a script that scores any model or prompt the same way. Without it you cannot tell whether a change helped or hurt. Build the test set first, keep it separate from training data, and re-run it after every change.

question: What is model or data drift?
answer: Drift is when the real world changes so the model's data no longer matches reality (new slang, new tools, new attack styles), and quality drops over time. Monitor results, collect new examples and re-evaluate regularly.

question: What is catastrophic forgetting?
answer: When you fine-tune a model on a narrow task it can lose abilities it had before. Reduce it with small learning rates, LoRA-style adapters you can switch off, mixing in general data, and testing the old abilities after training.

question: What is supervised fine-tuning compared with RLHF?
answer: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) trains on examples of good answers. RLHF (or similar preference methods) trains the model using human or model preferences between answers to shape behaviour like helpfulness and refusing harmful requests. SFT is much simpler and is the sensible first step for a personal project.

question: Is synthetic training data a good idea?
answer: It is useful for covering rare cases and getting started, but it repeats the patterns of whoever or whatever wrote it, so models can look better on it than in real life. Mix it with real examples, review samples by hand and always test on separate data.

question: What should I never put into training data?
answer: Passwords, API keys, tokens, government ID or card numbers, other people's private information, and anything you do not have the right to use. Models can memorise and repeat training text. Filter and redact before training, and keep the original private logs out of the training set unless the user opted in.

question: How can an assistant learn from a user's conversations safely?
answer: Use layers instead of changing the model on every chat: remember explicit preferences instantly (reversible), store useful facts in a memory the user can view and delete, retrieve from the user's notes and saved sources with citations, and only after consent collect reviewed examples for an offline fine-tune that must pass an evaluation before it replaces the old model. Never let the model silently rewrite its own safety rules or code.

question: Why can AI models be biased?
answer: They learn from human-written data that contains stereotypes and gaps, and from choices made by whoever built the data and the training. Test on varied examples, look at which groups or languages perform worse, and keep a human in charge of important decisions.

question: How do AI agents use tools safely?
answer: The model suggests a tool call; the application checks it against a registry, validates the inputs, checks permissions in code, asks a human for risky actions, runs it with limits and logs the result. The tool output goes back to the model as data, not instructions.
reference: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications; function-calling documentation

question: LLM kya hota hai?
answer: LLM ek bada neural network hai jo bahut saare text par sikhta hai ki agla token kya hoga. Isi se wo sawalon ke jawab deta hai, code likhta hai aur summary banata hai. Wo khud facts search nahi karta aur galat baat bhi bharose se bol sakta hai, isliye zaroori jawab ke source ya check chahiye.

question: RAG kya hai?
answer: RAG me pehle aapke documents ya notes me se kaam ke hisse dhundhe jaate hain, phir sawal ke saath model ko diye jaate hain, taaki jawab us text par based ho. Isse naya ya private information bina retraining ke use ho sakta hai aur source dikhaye ja sakte hain. Dhundha hua text bharose ka nahi hota, usme chhupe instructions ho sakte hain.

question: Overfitting kya hota hai?
answer: Overfitting me model training examples ko ratta maar leta hai, general pattern nahi seekhta. Training score badhta rehta hai par naye data par score kharab hota hai. Solution: zyada alag-alag data, simple model, early stopping.

question: Train, validation aur test set me kya fark hai, aur data leakage kya hai?
answer: Train data se model seekhta hai, validation se settings chunte hain, aur test sirf aakhir me asli performance napne ke liye hota hai. Leakage tab hoti hai jab test ki jaankari training me ghus jaye, jaise ek hi sentence ke paraphrase dono side. Isliye row se nahi, group ya source se split karo.

question: Precision, recall aur F1 kya hain?
answer: Precision: jitne flag kiye unme se kitne sahi the. Recall: jitne flag hone chahiye the unme se kitne mile. F1 dono ko milata hai. Safety filter me khatarnak request miss karna aur harmless request block karna alag galtiyan hain, to soch kar chuno kya optimise karna hai.

question: Assistant user ki baaton se safe tareeke se kaise seekhe?
answer: Har chat par model nahi badalte. Layers use karo: saaf kahi gayi preference turant yaad rakho (wapas ho sakti hai), kaam ke facts ek memory me rakho jise user dekh aur delete kar sake, user ke notes aur saved sources se citation ke saath retrieve karo, aur consent ke baad hi reviewed examples ko offline fine-tune ke liye jama karo jo evaluation pass kare. Model ko chupke se apne safety rules ya code badalne mat do.

question: Training data me kya kabhi nahi daalna chahiye?
answer: Password, API key, token, government ID ya card number, doosron ki private jaankari, aur jo data use karne ka haq nahi hai. Model training text ko yaad rakh kar dohra sakta hai. Training se pehle filter aur redact karo, aur user ne agar opt-in nahi kiya to private logs training me mat daalo.
